title: Describing changes over time / Describir cambios a lo largo del tiempo
bridge: In ngillɗo, to describe changes, structures with 'get', 'become' and 'turn' are used, which in Pulaar are often translated as 'wonaade', 'hokki' or 'jokki'. Unlike Pulaar, English does not use the verb 'to be' with adjectives to indicate a change; instead, these specific verbs are employed. Additionally, English distinguishes between the present perfect ('have changed') and the simple past ('changed'), which does not exactly match the compound past and simple past of Pulaar. Spanish-speaking students tend to translate 'estoy más cansado' literally as 'I am more tired' instead of 'I have gotten more tired'.
rule: To express changes in English: 1) Use 'get' + adjective (or comparative) for gradual or temporary changes: 'get older', 'get better', 'get colder'. 2) Use 'become' + adjective/noun for more permanent or formal changes: 'become a teacher', 'become famous'. 3) Use 'turn' + color or adjective for visible state changes: 'turn red', 'turn pale'. 4) For physical state or health changes, 'grow' (to grow) and 'fall' (to fall) can also be used in fixed expressions: 'grow old', 'fall asleep'. 5) With 'used to', past situations that are no longer true are spoken about: 'I used to live here'. 6) With 'no longer' and 'still', states are compared: 'I no longer smoke', 'I still work here'. 7) The present perfect is used when the change is relevant in the present: 'The town has changed a lot'. Do not use 'to be' + adjective as in Pulaar: 'miɗo wonaade' is not 'I am tired' if you want to say you have become tired, but 'I have gotten tired'.

concept_examples.text: The city has changed a lot.
She became more confident after the course.
concept_examples.translation: O jokkiɗo faaɗo faaɗo ɗum nden.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi bɪˈkeɪm mɔːr ˈkɑːnfɪdənt ˈæftər ðə kɔːrs/

concept_examples.text: The leaves turn yellow in autumn.

common_error.wrong: I am more tired now than before.
common_error.correct: I have gotten more tired now.
common_error.correct_alt: I have become more tired now.
common_error.explanation: The error occurs because in Pulaar one says 'miɗo wonaade' to indicate a change of state. But in English, 'I am tired' describes the current state, not the change. To express that there has been a change, you must use the present perfect with 'get' or 'become' (or 'have gotten' / 'have become'). You can say 'I am more tired' only if you are comparing with another moment, but it does not imply a process of change. Avoid literal translation and think about whether you are describing a state or a change.

examples.original: It is getting colder.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈɡetɪŋ ˈkoʊldər/
examples.translation: O wonaade faaɗo (o wonaade faaɗo).
examples.note: Use 'get' + comparative for gradual changes. In Pulaar, the continuous present 'o wonaade' is sometimes used, but in English 'is getting' can also be used.

examples.original: My English is getting better.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ˈɡetɪŋ ˈbɛtər/
examples.translation: Ingliisɗo am o wonaade faaɗo (o wonaade faaɗo).
examples.note: Here 'get better' is equivalent to 'mejorar' in Pulaar. Do not confuse with 'ser mejor'.

examples.original: The days are getting longer.
examples.phonetic: /ðə deɪz ɑːr ˈɡetɪŋ ˈlɔːŋɡər/
examples.translation: Deɗɗe o wonaade faaɗo (o wonaade faaɗo).
examples.note: Remember that 'long' is one syllable, but the comparative is 'longer' with -er.

examples.original: He became famous after the video.
examples.phonetic: /hi bɪˈkeɪm ˈfeɪməs ˈæftər ðə ˈvɪdi.oʊ/
examples.translation: O hokkiɗo famaamaɗo ɗum nden.
examples.note: Para cambios de estatus (famoso, rico) se prefiere 'become'. En español se dice 'hacerse'.

examples.original: The situation became complicated.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən bɪˈkeɪm ˈkɑːmplɪkeɪtɪd/
examples.translation: Haalɗo o hokkiɗo faaɗo.
examples.note: Aquí 'become complicated' equivale a 'volverse complicado'.

examples.original: She became a doctor in 2010.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi bɪˈkeɪm ə ˈdɑːktər ɪn tuː ˈθaʊzənd ˈtɛn/
examples.translation: O hokkiɗo doftorɗo ɗum 2010.
examples.note: Con profesiones o roles, se usa 'become' + sustantivo sin artículo.

levels.label: Expressing changes with used to and no longer
levels.translation: Expressing changes with used to and no longer

examples.original: I used to live in Madrid.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ juːst tʊ lɪv ɪn məˈdrɪd/
examples.translation: Miɗo wadiiɗo o yiɗɗo e Madrid.
examples.note: Para describir hábitos o estados pasados que ya no son ciertos, se usa 'used to' + verbo base.

examples.original: I no longer eat meat.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ noʊ ˈlɔːŋɡər iːt miːt/
examples.translation: Miɗo no longer yiɗɗo nyiiri.
examples.note: En español se usa 'ya no', en inglés 'no longer' es más formal que 'don't... anymore'.

examples.original: She didn't use to smoke, but now she does.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi ˈdɪdnt juːst tʊ smoʊk bʌt naʊ ʃi dʌz/
examples.translation: O didn't use to yiɗɗo nyiiri, ɓuri o yiɗɗo.
examples.note: En negativo se usa 'didn't use to' (sin -d final en 'use'). Cuidado con la pronunciación: /juːst/.

translations.ff: Describir cambios a lo largo del tiempo

title: Speculating and making deductions / Especular e jangu jangu
bridge: En pulaar, moƴƴe 'debe de ser' ko 'peeɗe to be' mo jangu jangu. En inglise, moƴƴe modale 'must', 'might', 'could', 'can't' + infinitif. Hakkunde, 'must' jangu jangu (wonaa ko wonaa), 'can't' jangu jangu (wonaa ko wonaa), 'might', 'may' ko 'could' jangu jangu (wonaa ko wonaa). Jokko: 'must not' wonaa ko jangu jangu, ko 'must not' wonaa ko laawol (prohibición).
rule: Ko jangu jangu en presente, moƴƴe modale bee yiide kaƴƴe verbe: 'must' (jangu jangu), 'can't' (jangu jangu ko wonaa), 'might', 'may', 'could' (jangu jangu, wonaa ko wonaa). Ko jangu jangu en pasado, moƴƴe 'must have + participio', 'can't have + participio', 'might have + participio', etc. Hakkunde: sujet + modal + verbe base (presente) ko modal + have + participio (pasado). Jokko: en pulaar, 'debe de ser' ko 'no puede ser' jangu jangu, ko inglise, 'must not be' wonaa ko jangu jangu, moƴƴe 'can't be'.

concept_examples.text: He must be tired after the long trip.
concept_examples.translation: O must be tired after the long journey.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst biː ˈtaɪərd ˈæftər ðə lɔːŋ trɪp/

concept_examples.text: She can't be serious about moving to another country.
concept_examples.translation: O can't be serious about moving to another country.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː kænt biː ˈsɪriəs əˈbaʊt ˈmuːvɪŋ tuː əˈnʌðər ˈkʌntri/

concept_examples.text: They might have forgotten the meeting.
concept_examples.translation: O might have forgotten the meeting.

concept_examples.text: It could rain later, so take an umbrella.
concept_examples.translation: O could rain later, so take an umbrella.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt kʊd reɪn ˈleɪtər soʊ teɪk ən ʌmˈbrelə/

common_error.wrong: He must not be at home because the lights are off.
common_error.correct: He can't be at home because the lights are off.
common_error.correct_alt: He must be out because the lights are off.
common_error.explanation: Halkere e pulaar, moƴƴe 'no debe estar' ko jangu jangu, ko inglise, 'must not' wonaa ko laawol (prohibición). Ko jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa, moƴƴe 'can't' (ko 'couldn't' ko laawol). Alternative 'must be out' jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa: jangu jangu ko o wonaa a home.

levels.label: Deductions with must and can't
levels.translation: Jangu jangu ko must e can't

examples.original: You're a journalist. You must meet a lot of people.
examples.phonetic: /jʊər ə ˈdʒɜːrnəlɪst. juː mʌst miːt ə lɒt əv ˈpiːpl/
examples.translation: Aaɗam naa journalist. O must know many people.
examples.note: Moƴƴe 'must' ko o jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa. En pulaar, 'debe de'.

examples.original: That can't be the right answer.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt kænt biː ðə raɪt ˈænsər/
examples.translation: O can't be the correct answer.
examples.note: Moƴƴe 'can't' ko wonaa ko wonaa. En pulaar, 'no puede ser'.

examples.original: He must have a lot of money because he drives a Ferrari.
examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst hæv ə lɒt əv ˈmʌni bɪˈkɒz hiː draɪvz ə fəˈrɑːri/
examples.translation: O must have a lot of money because o drives a Ferrari.
examples.note: Hakkunde moƴƴe 'because' (ko wonaa) mo jangu jangu.

levels.label: Possibility with might, may, and could
levels.translation: Jangu jangu ko might, may e could

examples.original: She might be at the gym right now.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː maɪt biː æt ðə dʒɪm raɪt naʊ/
examples.translation: O might be at the gym right now.
examples.note: 'Might' jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa ko 'must'. En pulaar, 'peeɗe to be'.

examples.original: They may arrive late because of the traffic.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ meɪ əˈraɪv leɪt bɪˈkɒz əv ðə ˈtræfɪk/
examples.translation: O may arrive late because of traffic.
examples.note: 'May' jangu jangu ko 'might', ko ko laawol ko laawol.

examples.original: This could be the best restaurant in the city.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs kʊd biː ðə best ˈrestərɒnt ɪn ðə ˈsɪti/
examples.translation: O could be the best restaurant in the city.
examples.note: 'Could' jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa moƴƴe 'might'.

levels.label: Deductions about the past
levels.translation: Jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa

examples.original: He must have studied a lot for the exam.
examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst hæv ˈstʌdid ə lɒt fɔːr ði ɪɡˈzæm/
examples.translation: O must have studied a lot for the exam.
examples.note: Moƴƴe 'must have + participio' ko jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa. En pulaar, 'debe de haber'.

examples.original: She can't have seen us because she didn't wave.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː kænt hæv siːn ʌs bɪˈkɒz ʃiː dɪdnt weɪv/
examples.translation: O can't have seen us because o didn't greet.
examples.note: 'Can't have + participio' jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa. En pulaar, 'no puede haber'.

examples.original: They might have missed the bus.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ maɪt hæv mɪst ðə bʌs/
examples.translation: O might have missed the bus.
examples.note: 'Might have + participio' jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa. En pulaar, 'peeɗe to have'.

examples.original: The roads are wet. It must have rained.
examples.phonetic: /ðə roʊdz ɑːr wet. ɪt mʌst hæv reɪnd/
examples.translation: The roads are wet. O must have rained.
examples.note: Hakkunde moƴƴe 'because' (ko wonaa) mo jangu jangu ko wonaa ko wonaa.

title: Expressing regret and hypothetical situations / Expresar arrepentimiento e hipótesis
bridge: En Pulaar, waxaad isticmaasay waaɗo e subjunctive si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha wax ku ool e waxba (misaal, 'ina hada waɗo, lahaa'). Aduuniyadda Ingiriis, qaabka waa kala duwan: waxaad isticmaasay 'past simple' (ama 'past perfect') ayaa ka mid ah 'if clause' iyo 'would' + verb ayaa ka mid ah 'main clause'. Faahfaahin caali ah waa in 'if I would have' loo turjumaado 'ina hada', laakiin ayaa ka mid ah 'if clause' ma leh 'would'. Waxa kale oo ah, si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha aan dhakista ahayn, waxaad isticmaasay 'past perfect' ('had + participle') ayaa ka mid ah 'if clause' iyo 'would have + participle' ayaa ka mid ah 'main clause'.
rule: Aduuniyadda Ingiriis B1, si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha wax ku ool e waxba (condicional nafarkeed) waxaad isticmaasay 'if + past simple' (ama 'if + past continuous') ayaa ka mid ah 'if clause', iyo 'would + base form' ayaa ka mid ah 'main clause'. Misale: 'If I had more time, I would travel.' (Ina hada waɗo, lahaa safar). Fadlan, 'were' waxaad isticmaasay dhammaan nafarkeed ayaa ka mid ah 'if I were' (waxaa kale oo 'was' ayaa loo isticmaalaa Ingiriis afafka casriga ah). Si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha aan dhakista ahayn (condicional nafarkeed ee saddexaad), waxaad isticmaasay 'if + past perfect' (had + participle) iyo 'would have + participle' ayaa ka mid ah 'main clause': 'If I had studied, I would have passed.' (Ina hada waxaan baranayey, lahaa inaan guuleysto). Waxa kale oo aad isticmaasay 'I wish' + past perfect si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha aan dhakista ahayn: 'I wish I had studied.' (Ina hada waxaan baranayey). Fadlan, 'if clause' ma leh 'would' ama 'will'. Ayaa ka mid ah waxyaabaha wax ku ool e, 'were' waxaad isticmaasay dhammaan nafarkeed: 'If he were here...'.

concept_examples.text: If I had more money, I would buy a car.
concept_examples.translation: Ina hada waɗo lacag, lahaa galle.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd mɔːr ˈmʌni aɪ wʊd baɪ ə kɑːr/

concept_examples.text: I wish I knew the answer.
If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
concept_examples.translation: Ina hada ay la baranay, lahaa inay guuleysay imtixaanka.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf ʃiː hæd ˈstʌdid ˈhɑːrdər ʃiː wʊd hæv pæst ði ɪɡˈzæm/

concept_examples.text: I would travel more if I were younger.
concept_examples.translation: Lahelaa safar si inay lahe nafay.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd ˈtrævl mɔːr ɪf aɪ wɜːr ˈjʌŋɡər/

common_error.wrong: If I would have time, I would go to the party.
common_error.correct: If I had time, I would go to the party.
common_error.correct_alt: If I had time, I'd go to the party.
common_error.explanation: Faahfaahin caali ah waa in 'ina hada lahaa waɗo' (condicional), laakiin Ingiriis 'if clause' ma leh 'would'. Waxa kale oo ayaa ka mid ah 'if' ka dibna waxaad isticmaasay 'past simple' (si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha wax ku ool e waxba) ama 'past perfect' (si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha aan dhakista ahayn), iyo 'would' ayaa ka mid ah 'main clause'.

levels.label: Second conditional (present/future hypotheticals)
levels.translation: Condicional nafarkeed ee labaad (waxyaabaha wax ku ool e waxba)

examples.original: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ wʌn ðə ˈlɑːtəri aɪ wʊd ˈtrævl ðə wɜːrld/
examples.translation: Ina hada waɗo nafay, lahaa inaan safar yahdo dunya.
examples.note: Fadlan, 'won' waa 'past simple', maanaheedu ma aha 'guuleysay' halkan.

examples.original: If he were taller, he could play basketball.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf hiː wɜːr ˈtɔːlər hiː kʊd pleɪ ˈbæskɪtbɔːl/
examples.translation: Ina hada waɗo nafay, lahaa inaan jeclaan balon.
examples.note: Ingiriis casriga ah waxaad isticmaasay 'were' dhammaan nafarkeed, laakiin 'was' ayaa loo isticmaalaa casriga ah.

examples.original: What would you do if you had a million dollars?
examples.phonetic: /wʌt wʊd juː duː ɪf juː hæd ə ˈmɪljən ˈdɑːlərz/
examples.translation: Max lahelaa si inay lahe dolla amma?
examples.note: Su'aasha waxaad beddelaysaa 'would' iyo nafarka.

levels.label: Third conditional (past regret)
levels.translation: Condicional nafarkeed ee saddexaad (arrepentimiento ayaa ka mid ah dhakista ahayn)

examples.original: If I had known, I would have come earlier.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd noʊn aɪ wʊd hæv kʌm ˈɜːrliər/
examples.translation: Ina hada ay la baranayey, lahaa inay yimme e halkan ka hor.
examples.note: Waxaad isticmaasay 'past perfect' (had + participle) ayaa ka mid ah 'if clause' iyo 'would have + participle' ayaa ka mid ah 'main clause'.

examples.original: She wouldn't have missed the train if she had left home on time.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˈwʊdnt hæv mɪst ðə treɪn ɪf ʃiː hæd left hoʊm ɒn taɪm/
examples.translation: Ay ma guuleysay inay teeru la teerey si ay la teerey gida.
examples.note: Waxa kale oo aad isticmaasay 'would not' oo loo qoro 'wouldn't'.

examples.original: If we had booked in advance, we would have got a discount.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wiː hæd bʊkt ɪn ədˈvɑːns wiː wʊd hæv ɡɒt ə ˈdɪskaʊnt/
examples.translation: Ina hada ay la teerey waɗo, lahaa inay heysay rabat.
examples.note: Ingiriis brittaniya waxaad isticmaasay 'got' oo loo isticmaalaa participle; Ingiriis mareykanka ayaa kale oo ayaa isticmaalaa 'gotten'.

examples.original: I wish I had studied more for the test.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ hæd ˈstʌdid mɔːr fər ðə test/
examples.translation: Ina hada ay la baranayey si inay lahe awoodo jawabu imtixaanka.
examples.note: Waxaad isticmaasay 'wish' + past perfect si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha aan dhakista ahayn.

examples.original: I wish I could speak English fluently.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ kʊd spiːk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluːəntli/
examples.translation: Ina hada ayaan awoodo Ingiriis si aad ugu hadlo siid.
examples.note: Waxaad isticmaasay 'could' + verb si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha awoodaha ayaa ka mid ah waqtigaada.

examples.original: I wish it weren't raining today.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ ɪt wɜːrnt ˈreɪnɪŋ təˈdeɪ/
examples.translation: Ina hada ay la teerey si aad ugu hadlo waqtigaada.
examples.note: Waxaad isticmaasay 'wish' + past continuous si aad ugu hadli lahayd waxyaabaha ayaa ka mid ah waqtigaada.
